editorial:
You follow a crew of small-time thieves hired to break into a quiet house and steal one rare VHS tape. Instead, they find a pile of strange recordings and a dead body. Each tape shows a different scary story, from a night out gone wrong to a road trip that turns deadly. The movie feels rough, messy, and unpredictable, like you are watching something you were not supposed to see. It is not polished, but that raw style is part of the fun.

The acting is natural enough to sell the chaos, and the pacing keeps jumping between stories before you get bored. Some segments are stronger than others, and the shaky camera can be tiring. Still, if you like horror anthologies and found footage, this is a good pick. Watch it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, rent it on Apple TV, or grab the 4K Blu-ray for the best picture.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, the thief watching the tapes is attacked after the old man in the chair disappears. The last recording shows friends entering the wrong house on Halloween and getting pulled into a deadly ritual. The twist is that the tapes are not just stories; they are bait. By watching them, the thief becomes part of the collection, and the cycle starts again for the next person who finds the house.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves found footage horror and short scary stories.
